memory_update.text: SPSC is the cleanest US-listed pure-play candidate for retail trading-partner networks, with 2025 filings supporting a direct link to retail/grocery/distribution/supplier EDI infrastructure and 96% recurring revenue.

OTEX is a diversified but relevant B2B integration and EDI network candidate; Business Network / Trading Grid purity must be isolated from broader OpenText segments before it can rank highly in later layers.
DSGX is an adjacent logistics/trade-network candidate rather than pure retail EDI; include for second-order exposure to retail/ecommerce shipment, customs, and logistics-data workflows.

CMRC is a speculative below-USD-300M exception via Feedonomics/BigCommerce marketplace and product-feed integrations; only survives if Feedonomics shows durable enterprise retention, ARR growth, and marketplace integration pull.

For retail trading-partner networks, the key chokepoint evidence is not just software functionality; it is the installed map of retailers, suppliers, message standards, compliance rules, ASN/invoice/order workflows, ERP integrations, and testing/onboarding friction.

Layer 2 should verify whether public filings disclose customer concentration, recurring revenue quality, net revenue retention, gross retention, customer count, ARPU, transaction volume, and vertical mix by retail/grocery/apparel/CPG/ecommerce.

node: Retail EDI and trading-partner compliance networks
summary: Expanded the universe around retail EDI, B2B integration, trading-partner compliance, and adjacent product/order data networks. The strongest direct public-market fit is SPS Commerce, which appears unusually pure for this node. OpenText and Descartes provide broader B2B/trading-partner networks with retail relevance but lower purity. Commerce.com is a speculative below-USD-300M exception because Feedonomics/BigCommerce sit adjacent to marketplace/product-feed integrations rather than classic EDI compliance. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
